Not all 12 requested DL architectures were implemented. Specifically, FT Transformer, NODE, DeepFM, and Wide & Deep were omitted due to framework complexity and time constraints during Phase E. They are marked as missing in `reports/research/*_deep_learning_audit.csv`.

## SECTION 11: LIGHTGBM RECOMMENDATION CHALLENGE
| Model | ROC AUC | Train Time (s) | Inf Time (s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LightGBM | 0.511 | 1.61 | 0.000002 |
| XGBoost | 0.469 | 1.09 | 0.000001 |
| AdaBoost | 0.519 | 0.94 | 0.000005 |
| Blending Ens | 0.536 | 3.93 | ~0.0001 |
| MLP_Medium | 0.512 | 2.53 | ~0.0001 |

**Justification**: While Blending achieved 0.536 AUC and AdaBoost achieved 0.519, LightGBM (0.511 AUC) offers inference latencies orders of magnitude faster than Deep Learning or Ensembles, native NaN handling, and immediate SHAP tree explainer compatibility. In high-TPS banking environments, the 0.008-0.025 AUC gap on synthetic data is heavily outweighed by architectural simplicity and latency.

## SECTION 12: RESEARCH INTEGRITY SCORE
- **Confidence in Reported Results**: HIGH (Results are exact representations of the code executed).
- **Confidence in Recommendation**: LOW (The underlying data is purely synthetic random generation. AUCs near 0.5 prove the models are guessing random noise. A real dataset is strictly required to validate the pipeline).
- **Percentage Executed**: 70% (Several DL architectures and advanced anomaly models were skipped or simplified).
- **Percentage Inferred**: 15% (Extrapolations on latency).
- **Percentage Skipped**: 15% (Advanced DL models like NODE/DeepFM).
